               <ns0:p n="50">50 And they all forsook him, and fled.<ns0:note place="bottom">Having to compleat the History of the Passion, especially as to what is said of it by <ns0:hi>Matthew, Mark,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Luke,</ns0:hi> in my Notes on <ns0:hi>Matthew,</ns0:hi> considered all passages relating to what <ns0:hi>Matthew</ns0:hi> saith, the things here mentioned being opened in our Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 26.47, 48, 49.50. need not here again be inlarged upon.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="51">51 And there followed him a certain young man, having a linnen cloth cast about his naked body, and the young men laid hold on him.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="52">52 And he left the linnen cloth, and fled from them naked.<ns0:note place="bottom">This part of the History is only recorded by <ns0:hi>Mark:</ns0:hi> what hath made some affirm that this was St. <ns0:hi>Iohn,</ns0:hi> I cannot tell. <ns0:hi>Iohn</ns0:hi> was one of the <ns0:hi>eleven,</ns0:hi> that were with Christ, when <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> came, and tho we find him asleep a little before, yet we read not that he was gone to bed, nor can conceive there was any, at or near the place. The garment in which he was, in all probability, was a <ns0:hi>Night garment.</ns0:hi> It is certain it was a loose garment, he could not else when he was apprehended, have so soon quit himself of it, and being quit of that it seemeth he was quit of all, for the Text saith, <ns0:hi>he fled from them naked,</ns0:hi> nor doth the Text give him the honour to call him a <ns0:hi>Disciple of Christ</ns0:hi> at large. Probably, it was some young man, who being in his Bed, and hearing the noise of the multitude, going by his lodging with Swords and Staves, got up, slipt on his <ns0:hi>Night garment,</ns0:hi> and followed them, to see what the matter was, and they having apprehended Christ, he followed them. And possibly his unusual habit, made them take the more notice of him, staying when the Disciples were all fled. Nor can the reason be well given why <ns0:hi>Mark</ns0:hi> should record such a passage, unless it were to tell us what we must expect, from the <ns0:hi>rage</ns0:hi> of Persecutors, <ns0:hi>viz. That our own innocency should not defend us.</ns0:hi> This young Man was not concerned in Christ, only came as a Spectator, without any Arms. But the <ns0:hi>Sword</ns0:hi> of <ns0:hi>Persecution,</ns0:hi> useth not to distinguish perfectly. The <ns0:hi>Basilisk</ns0:hi> (they say) will fly at the picture of a Man.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="53">53 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 22.54.63, 64. John 18.19.</ns0:note> And they led Jesus away to the high priest, and with him were assembled all the chief priests, and the elders, and the scribes.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="54">54 And Peter followed him afar off, even into the palace of the high priest, and he sat with the servants, and warmed himself at the fire.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="55">55 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matth. 26.59.</ns0:note> And the chief priests, and all the council sought for witness against Jesus to put him to death; and found none.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="56">56 For many bare false witness against him, but their witness agreed not together.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="57">57 And there arose certain, and bare false witness against him, saying,</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="58">58 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Chap. 15.23. John 2.19.</ns0:note> We heard him say, I will destroy this temple that is made with hands, and within three days I will build another made without hands.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="59">59 But neither so did their witness agree toge<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ther.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="60">60 And the high priest stood up in the mids, and asked Jesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? what is it which these witness against thee?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="61">61 But he held his peace, and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Isa. 53.7.</ns0:note> answered nothing. Again the high priest asked him, and said unto him, Art thou the Christ the Son of the Blessed?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="62">62 And Jesus said, I am: and <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Matth. 24.32.</ns0:note> ye shall see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of Power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="63">63 Then the high priest rent his clothes, and said, What need we any further witnesses?</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="64">64 Ye have heard the blasphemy: what think ye? And they all condemned him to be guilty of death.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="65">65 And some began to spit on him, and to cover his face, and to buffet him, and to say unto him, Prophesie, And the servants did strike him with the palms of their hands.<ns0:note place="bottom">This History of our Saviours examination before the <ns0:hi>High Priest</ns0:hi> we had <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 26. from <ns0:hi>v.</ns0:hi> 57. to 69. See the Notes there. It should seem the <ns0:hi>High Priests,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Council</ns0:hi> were very eager upon this thing. This Council seems to have sat up all Night, for early in the Morning they carried him (condemned by them) to <ns0:hi>Pilate,</ns0:hi> and before twelve, they brought him out of the City to be Cruci<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />fied. These wretched <ns0:hi>Hypocrites,</ns0:hi> had but the evening before been taking the <ns0:hi>Passover.</ns0:hi> It was now the <ns0:hi>Feast of Vnleavened Bread.</ns0:hi> This was now the first Fruit of their thanksgiving to God, for bringing them out of the Land of <ns0:hi>Aegypt.</ns0:hi> Besides that their keeping a Court of Judgment in a capital case, on an <ns0:hi>Holy<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />day,</ns0:hi> or <ns0:hi>in the Night,</ns0:hi> were things against all <ns0:hi>rules of order.</ns0:hi> But the rage of Persecutors can be neither bounded by the Laws of God or Men. If the Servants of God still be thus treated, they are in this more like Christ, who hath told them, <ns0:hi>That the Dis<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />ciple is not above his Master.</ns0:hi> But see further in the <ns0:hi>Notes</ns0:hi> on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 26.</ns0:note>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="66">66 <ns0:note n="*" place="margin">Luke 22.<ns0:gap reason="illegible" resp="#PDCC" extent="1 letter">

                     </ns0:gap>.23.</ns0:note> And as Peter was beneath in the palace, there cometh one of the maids of the high priest.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="67">67 And when she saw Peter warming himself, she looked upon him, and said, And thou also wast with Jesus of Nazareth.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="68">68 But he denied, saying, I know not, neither understand I what thou sayest. And he went out into the porch; and the cock crew.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="69">69 And a maid saw him again, and began to say to them that stood by, This is <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> of them.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="70">70 And he denied it again. And a little after, they that stood by said again to Peter, Surely thou art <ns0:hi>one</ns0:hi> of them: for thou art a Galilean, and thy speech agreeth <ns0:hi>thereto.</ns0:hi>
               </ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="71">71 But he began to curse and to swear, <ns0:hi>saying,</ns0:hi> I know not this man of whom ye speak.</ns0:p>
               <ns0:p n="72">72 And the second time the cock crew. And Peter called to mind the word that Jesus said unto him, Before the cock crow twice, thou shalt deny me thrice.                         </ns0:gap>.</ns0:hi> Or, <ns0:hi>he began weep.</ns0:hi>
                  </ns0:note>.<ns0:note place="bottom">All four Evangelists give us an account of this History of <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi>'s denial of his Master. We have considered what they all say to compleat the History, in our Notes on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 26.69, 70, 71, 72, <ns0:hi>&c.</ns0:hi> To which I see no reason to add any thing but the observation. 1. <ns0:hi>How contemptible means God often useth to take down our Pride, and self-confidences. Peter</ns0:hi> a great Apostle is here humbled by the means of two Maids. 2. <ns0:hi>How naturally one Sin draws on another. Peter</ns0:hi> first telleth a Lye, then to <ns0:hi>Lying,</ns0:hi> addeth <ns0:hi>Swearing,</ns0:hi> and <ns0:hi>Cursing.</ns0:hi> 3. <ns0:hi>How necessary it is for those that would keep from Sin, to keep out of Sinners company.</ns0:hi> I am (saith <ns0:hi>David) a companion of them that fear thee.</ns0:hi> 4. <ns0:hi>How profitable Words from God are for the time to come,</ns0:hi> tho at pre<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sent we find not the use, and advantage of them. 5. <ns0:hi>How diffe<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />rent the Sinnings of Reprobates, and Saints are,</ns0:hi> as to the <ns0:hi>con<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />sequences</ns0:hi> and issues. <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> Sins, repents, and hangs himself. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> goeth out and weepeth bitterly. <ns0:hi>Iudas</ns0:hi> repented unto Death. <ns0:hi>Peter</ns0:hi> repenteth unto Life. See more with reference to this History, in our <ns0:hi>Notes</ns0:hi> on <ns0:hi>Matth.</ns0:hi> 26.75. Thus far we have heard Christs trial, before the <ns0:hi>Ecclesiastical Court</ns0:hi> of the <ns0:hi>Iews.</ns0:hi> Thus far what he said <ns0:hi>Chap.</ns0:hi> 10.33. is made good. <ns0:hi>He is deli<ns0:g ref="char:EOLhyphen" />vered to the chief Priests, and the Scribes, and they have</ns0:hi> (as we have heard) <ns0:hi>condemned him to Death,</ns0:hi> but he also said there.—<ns0:hi>And they shall deliver him to the Gentiles, And they shall mock him, and shall scourge him, and shall spit upon him, and shall kill him.</ns0:hi> We must see those Words verified in the insuing part of the History, in the next Chapter.</ns0:note>
